summary:
Our project, “Forgotten in Space: Exploring NASA’s Abandoned Space Technologies and Their Scientific Legacy,” is an educational website that explores NASA hardware left across the solar system since the 1960s. We developed an interactive platform where visitors can discover different spacecraft, rovers, landers, and other technologies, learn where they were sent, understand their original purposes, and explore what happened to them after their missions ended.

The website addresses NASA’s challenge by bringing together the stories of space equipment that was intentionally left behind, became inactive, or completed its mission. It highlights the scientific discoveries and technological achievements made possible by these missions, while distinguishing retired equipment from spacecraft that are still operating.

This project is important because these technologies are more than forgotten objects: they represent decades of exploration, innovation, and scientific progress. By sharing their stories in an engaging and accessible way, we hope to inspire curiosity about space exploration and help people appreciate the lasting impact of NASA’s missions.
details:
Project Details: Forgotten in Space

Our project, “Forgotten in Space,” is a website about NASA's old spacecraft, rovers, landers, and other equipment that have been left behind in space or on other planets. We wanted to explore what happened to these technologies after their missions ended and what they helped us discover.

What does it do and how does it work?

Our website allows visitors to explore different NASA missions and the equipment used in them. They can learn when and where each spacecraft or rover was sent, what its purpose was, what discoveries it made, and why its mission ended. We also include pictures and useful information to make everything easier to understand.

What are its benefits?

It helps students and other visitors learn about space exploration in an interesting way. It also brings information about different NASA missions together in one place, so people don't have to search through many websites to learn about them.

What is the intended impact?

We want people to understand that even though some space missions have ended, the discoveries they made are still important. We also hope our project encourages students to become more interested in space, science, and technology.

What tools and technologies did we use?

We used Python and Flask to build the website, HTML to create the pages, CSS to design them, and JavaScript to add interactive features. We used SQLite to store information about the missions and NASA's Image and Video Library API to find space-related pictures. We also used Visual Studio Code to write our code and GitHub to manage our project.

How is the project creative?

Instead of focusing only on famous and currently active space missions, we chose to look at the equipment that was left behind after missions ended. We thought it would be interesting to show what happened to these machines and how they helped NASA learn more about the solar system.

What factors did our team consider?

We focused on making the website easy to use and understand. We also considered the accuracy of the information, the quality of the pictures, and how to organize the content so visitors could find what they were looking for. Another important point was explaining the difference between equipment that was abandoned, equipment that stopped working, and missions that simply came to an end.

Through this project, we want to show that even the machines left behind in space have stories worth learning about.
